Ukraine Military Aid Surged in June Despite Long-Term Shortages: Institute — EU financing pushed military aid for Ukraine to a 15-month high in June, with Kyiv receiving €7.2 billion ($8.3 billion). But despite the surge, Europe’s long-term support remains below pre-2025 levels as the US role in arming Ukraine declines.

Russia Launches 133 Drones at Ukraine Overnight, Killing Two Railway Workers — Russian forces launched 133 drones at Ukraine overnight on Thursday, with Ukrainian air defenses intercepting 111, according to the Ukrainian Air Force. Strikes hit 15 locations, while debris fell in 16 others. Two railway workers were killed when a jet-powered drone struck a passenger train locomotive in Odesa region, while five people were wounded in Dnipropetrovsk region and another in Zaporizhzhia.

Zelensky Says 5% of US Patriot Missiles Could Save Ukraine This Winter — President Volodymyr Zelensky told CNN that Ukraine urgently needs more US Patriot interceptors as Russia increases its ballistic missile attacks. He said Ukraine currently has only 1% of the US stockpile, while 5% could help Kyiv survive the winter and 10% could enable it to stop all Russian ballistic missiles.

Putin Visits Disputed Kuril Islands for First Time as Russia-Japan Tensions Deepen — Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands highlights deepening Russia-Japan tensions as Tokyo continues backing Ukraine.

Ukraine for First Time Combines 15 Weapons in Novorossiysk Strike, Expanding Black Sea ‘No-Go Zone’ — Ukraine combined 15 domestically produced weapons in a coordinated strike on Novorossiysk, hitting Russian warships and prompting authorities to declare a state of emergency in the Black Sea port city.

Karoline Leavitt to Step Down as White House Press Secretary — Karoline Leavitt will step down as White House press secretary at the end of August to focus on her family while remaining a senior outside advisor to Trump.

US Senators Press Rubio, Bessent Over 17-Month Pause in Russia Sanctions — US Senators Warren and Coons are pressing Rubio and Bessent to explain why routine Russia counter-evasion sanctions remain paused despite stalled peace talks and continued sanctions evasion.

Zelensky Says Armenia Ties Are ‘Even More Constructive’ as Putin Stays Silent on Pashinyan Victory — Zelensky and Pashinyan discussed closer Ukraine-Armenia cooperation amid growing strains between Armenia and Russia.

Estonia Pledges Nearly $400,000 for Ukraine’s Winter Preparation — Estonia’s Foreign Ministry announced €340,000 ($392,000) in aid to help Ukraine prepare for another winter of war, with Russia widely expected to strike the country’s energy and water infrastructure. The funds will be allocated to frontline families, displaced Ukrainians, and rescuers through non-governmental organization (NGO) partners.

4 Russian Warships Struck in Novorossiysk — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported that four Russian warships sustained damage during an overnight operation at the Novorossiysk naval base. Damage assessments are ongoing.

Zaporizhzhia Firefighter Killed in ‘Double-Tap’ Strike — A firefighter with over 20 years in service was killed in a “double-tap” attack – a technique Russia uses to target first responders and emergency services following an earlier strike. Two other emergency responders were injured in the attack as crews attended the scene of of an initial hit.

Zelensky Says Ukraine Must Give its Youth ‘Reasons to Stay’ — President Volodymyr Zelensky marked Ukraine’s Youth Day by calling for stronger government attention to youth policy. The new Cabinet of Ministers is tasked to give young people in Ukraine concrete reasons to stay and build futures in the country, according to Zelensky, as Ukraine approaches its fifth year of war and faces deep uncertainty.

2 Russian Prison Officers Accused of Torturing Ukrainian Detainees — The Prosecutor General’s Office has accused two Russian prison staff of torturing Ukrainian civilians held in a Kursk detention center. Investigators reportedly documented electric shock and beatings against at least five victims.

Vučić Welcomes Zelensky in Serbia: Turning Point or Tactical Gambit? — Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić has been alternately hot and cold in his relationship with Moscow, a traditional Serbian ally. After Zelensky’s visit to Belgrade, Vučić’s motives are facing increased scrutiny.

Ukrainian Air Assault Forces Liberate 26 Settlements in 3 Regions — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced the liberation of 26 settlements across three regions, crediting Ukraine’s Air Assault Forces (DSHV) and all other units involved. According to DSHV, Russian losses totaled more than 9,550 troops killed since January.

Emergency Declared in Novorossiysk After Ukrainian Strike on Russian Naval Base — Russian authorities declared an emergency after the attack ruptured two water pipelines, sparked fires and disrupted port operations. Ukraine reported hitting air defenses, naval piers and infrastructure at the Novorossiysk base.

Kyiv Prepares Lists of Residents Who May Need Evacuation in Winter — Kyiv authorities are compiling lists of residents who may need temporary relocation if Russian strikes cause prolonged heating outages this winter. The initiative focuses on people with limited mobility, including elderly residents living alone, people with disabilities and families raising children with disabilities.

Ukraine Finds Nvidia AI Chip in New Russian Missile, HUR Says — Ukraine's military intelligence says specialists identified an Nvidia Jetson Orin computer module among the components of Russia's new S-71 Monochrome cruise missile. The HUR also identified 35 foreign electronic components in Russian weapons.

Russia Produces 3,000 Geran-4/5 Drones a Month, Ukraine Says — Russia's defense industry produces around 3,000 Geran-4 and Geran-5 kamikaze drones each month, Ukraine's military intelligence told Militarnyi. Production is centered in Tatarstan, where Russia is also expanding facilities as it increases the use of faster jet-powered drones designed to challenge Ukrainian air defenses.

Russian Man Taken From Street, Pressured to Sign Army Contract, Relatives Say — The reported case comes amid growing evidence that Russian recruiters are using street raids, workplace visits and pressure on vulnerable men as Moscow struggles to attract enough volunteers for its war against Ukraine.

Russia Amasses 6,200 Kamikaze Drones for Armada Assault on Ukraine, HUR Says — Russia is building large drone reserves because its production capacity cannot sustain peak attack intensity continuously. HUR says Moscow launches fewer UAVs while replenishing stocks before unleashing much larger barrages.

Kremlin Removes Even Weak Opposition as Ukraine War Takes Toll — Yabloko’s removal from Russia’s parliamentary ballot comes as even state-linked pollsters record falling support for Vladimir Putin and the war in Ukraine. Yet the party’s history, internal divisions and some of its leaders’ statements about Ukraine illustrate why opposing Putin does not automatically make someone a reliable ally of Ukraine.

Putin’s Visit Brings Cheaper Petrol and Freshly Fixed Roads to Siberia — Putin’s visit to Siberia brought an unusual sight: petrol prices reportedly dropped as his motorcade passed through Novosibirsk. Residents also saw freshly repaired roads, heavy security and widespread restrictions – prompting some to joke that Putin should tour Russia nonstop.

HRW Urges US Congress to Block Turkey's Cluster Munitions Transfer to Ukraine — Human Rights Watch has urged the US Congress to block Turkey's proposed transfer of US-origin cluster munitions to Ukraine. The planned $256 million deal includes 70 ATACMS missiles, 2,524 M26 rockets and 47,000 artillery projectiles containing more than 10 million explosive submunitions.

Poles are Not ‘Second-Class’: Warsaw Demands Musk Restore Starlink Access — Poland has urged SpaceX to reverse Starlink’s exclusion of Polish customers from its European roaming zone, calling the policy discriminatory. The change could force Polish users to pay more for international use and complete additional formalities. Warsaw is demanding clear regulatory justification, while speculation links the decision to Poland’s Starlink support for Ukraine.

Kyiv Faces Second Drone Attack in a Day as Russian Strikes Continue Around the Clock — Kyiv came under a second Russian drone attack on Aug. 12, with air defenses engaging jet-powered drones approaching the capital from multiple directions. Kyiv Post team members across the city and surrounding villages reported hearing loud explosions as Russia continued its near-round-the-clock aerial strikes against Ukraine.

Ukraine Strikes Russia’s ‘Last’ Black Sea Fleet Stronghold in Novorossiysk — Ukraine says its forces carried out a major overnight strike on Russia’s naval base in Novorossiysk, hitting air defenses, piers, and port infrastructure more than 300 kilometers from the front line.

Vance Asked Zelensky to Avoid Key Oil Route as Ukraine Targets Russia’s Black Sea Fleet — Zelensky said Ukrainian forces struck Russian air defenses, naval piers, and port infrastructure in Novorossiysk. The operation came as the Financial Times reported that Kyiv had stopped attacks on vessels serving a major Kazakh oil terminal following a request from JD Vance.

Trump’s Envoys’ Kyiv Visit Will Embarrass Them & Offend Ukrainians | Bohdan Nahaylo — US President Donald Trump’s real estate mogul friend Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner, whom Trump has appointed as his special peace envoys, are expected to finally visit Kyiv, after already having met with Russian envoys several times, including in Moscow. Can their diplomatic efforts succeed in bringing Russia and Ukraine to the negotiating table?

Fires Erupt Across Russian-Occupied Crimea After Major Overnight Drone Attack — Large fires were reported at several locations in Russian-occupied Crimea following a major overnight drone attack Aug.11-12. Satellite imagery cited by the monitoring group Crimean Wind showed fires near Balaklava and at a Russian border military facility in northern Crimea, while Russian-installed officials acknowledged fires in Sevastopol.

Russian Strikes Hit Epicentr Store in Zaporizhzhia, Kill 2 in Kherson — Russia struck a shopping center in Zaporizhzhia overnight, a day after a deadly missile attack on the city that included North Korean-supplied ballistic missiles, Ukrainian officials said. The latest strike caused extensive damage to an Epicentr store, while overnight Russian attacks also killed two women in Kherson.

‘The Best Drone Is One That Never Rises’: Germany Mulls Cyberattacks on Russian Drone Makers — Germany is considering giving its intelligence services new powers to launch preemptive cyberattacks against Russian drone manufacturers, a senior lawmaker said. The proposal aims to disrupt threats before they reach Germany, but civil liberties groups warn the reforms could dramatically expand the powers of German intelligence agencies.

July Was Deadliest Month for Civilians in Ukraine Since 2022, Monitoring Group Says — At least 634 civilians were killed in July in strikes on civilian infrastructure, making it the deadliest month in at least 2.5 years, according to the Conflict Intelligence Team. More than 4,590 people were injured, with around 30% of the fatalities recorded in Russia or occupied Ukrainian territories.

North Korean-Supplied Missiles Attack Ukraine as Russia Escalates Air War — North Korean ballistic missiles struck Zaporizhzhia alongside Russian Zirkon missiles and glide bombs, killing six civilians and wounding 19. The attack highlights deepening Moscow–Pyongyang military ties and Ukraine’s air-defense shortages.

Traveling Through Poland to Ukraine: Observations of a Norwegian — Poland’s support for Ukraine increasingly clashes with domestic nationalism, anti-Ukrainian sentiment and political disputes that expose the country’s deeper strategic contradictions.

Zelensky: Ukraine Has Given US Envoys Proposals for Ending Russia’s War — Zelensky said Ukraine has given the US proposals for ending Russia’s war and urged Washington to strengthen air defense and increase pressure on Moscow.
Russian Drone Kills Woman Inside Her Home in Kherson — A woman was killed inside her home after a Russian drone struck Kherson overnight, local authorities reported.

The Domino Fear: Why a 2% Party Threatens Putin’s Endless War in Ukraine — Yabloko posed little electoral threat, but its anti-war platform risked turning scattered discontent into a visible political constituency against Russia’s war in Ukraine.

North Korea Fires Ballistic Missile 1 Day After Zelensky Warns Japan, South Korea, Philippines — Pyongyang launched a ballistic missile toward Japan shortly after Zelensky warned that North Korea’s deepening military cooperation with Russia threatens Japan, South Korea and the Philippines.

Romania Destroys 2 Russian-Made Drones Near Major Black Sea Gas Project — Romanian forces destroyed 2 Russian-made Gerbera drones near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project after they were found drifting in the Black Sea.

Russian Drone Hits 5-Story Residential Building in Odesa — A Russian drone damaged a fifth-floor apartment in Odesa, with no casualties reported, as Ukraine’s Air Force warned of further UAVs approaching the region.

Austria Uncovers Sanctions-Evasion Scheme Supplying Russian Military Industry — Austria’s interior ministry uncovered a sanctions-evasion network in which a Vienna-based company supplied equipment to Russia through hidden channels. The equipment was used to build Russian cruise missiles and fighter jet engines.

Ukraine Repels 185 Combat Clashes on Tuesday — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported 185 combat clashes over the past 24 hours, as Russian forces launched nearly 6,770 drones and 208 guided aerial bombs (KABs) nationwide.

Russia Preparing Mass Mobilization for Fall, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky cited a report from Ukraine’s Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR), saying that Russia is planning for a rapid mobilization of more than 100,000 troops to begin after Russia’s rigged parliamentary elections in September. Ukraine is preparing countermeasures.

Germany Grants Ukraine’s State Emergency Service Nearly €6M in Robotic Firefighting Package — Germany delivered a €5.7 million ($6.6 million) package of firefighting equipment to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (SES), including robotic systems and specialized vehicles. The transfer highlights Berlin’s support for Ukrainian emergency responders which began in 2015.

Here Comes the Sun — Col. Yevhen Konovalets represented a generation who refused to accept that Ukraine’s struggle for independence was over. He believed Ukraine would one day be free. Now his remains are coming back to Ukraine from Rotterdam, where he was assassinated by Moscow in 1938.

Russia Releases Ex-US Marine Robert Gilman After 4 Years — Russia released former US Marine Robert Gilman on Tuesday, Aug 11, after four years in captivity. Gilman was detained in January 2022, following an incident in Voronezh, where he allegedly assaulted a police officer. Gilman was flown to Washington, DC for medical treatment after a US senator described him as “catatonic.”

Russian Strikes Injure 1, Damage Homes Across Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian forces struck the Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 50 times on Tuesday, Aug. 11, injuring one woman and damaging private homes, a business, and local civilian infrastructure.

The Mecca Agreement – Q&A — The Mecca Agreement — a new Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey defense pact with NATO Article Five-like mutual defense provisions — reflects deepening distrust among former US allies after Washington's handling of the Iran war exposed gaps in its security guarantees. Saudi Arabia seeks diversified protection beyond US backing; Turkey and Pakistan gain access to Saudi financing for defense modernization. Egypt remains hesitant to join over UAE ties and Saudi rivalry, while Isra

Ukraine to Continue Youth Housing Reform Push — Prime Minister Serhii Koretsykii met with regional youth leaders on Tuesday, Aug. 11, marking the launch of a new consultative body called the Chamber of Regional Youth Congresses.

Russian Strikes Hit Kramatorsk Church, Sloviansk Market, 4 Injured — Russian strikes on Ukraine's Donetsk region on Tuesday, Aug. 11, set fire to the dome of a church in Kramatorsk and injured at least four people in Sloviansk, where Russian forces hit the central market at midday while people were there. Firefighters extinguished the church blaze covering 140 square meters, with no casualties reported at that site. Local officials said the market strike had no military logic and was intended to

Out of Patriots, Dead Generals, and a Reform From the Top — Ukraine's front lines remain largely static as Russian infiltration slows, though heavy fighting continues near Kostiantynivka-Druzhkivka. Russia struck Kyiv with unintercepted ballistic missiles amid Ukraine's Patriot shortage, killing 17. Ukraine's long-range campaign intensified: sinking the Yanina, disabling the Nadezhda ferry, and hitting Kerch ferries, refineries, and Wildberries warehouses nationwide. New AFU leadership is invest

Ukraine Warns Russia’s ‘Starlink Rival’ Could Open a New Drone Threat — A Ukrainian presidential adviser says Russia’s Rassvet network could improve battlefield communications and enable the real-time control of drones over Ukrainian territory.

US Sells 2 Seized Sanctioned Tankers for Scrap After Venezuela Raid — The US government has sold two sanctioned oil tankers seized in the days after Washington's raid on Venezuela to Dubai-headquartered recycling firm Global Marketing Systems, Lloyd's List reported. The Russian-flagged vessels, now named Era and Lileo, were seized in January and will be demolished in scrap yards in India.

Ukraine Stops Reporting Russian Missile Interceptions as Air Defense Struggles Intensify — Ukraine has stopped reporting Russian missile interception figures as Moscow intensifies ballistic strikes and Kyiv faces a growing shortage of air-defense interceptors. With Patriot missiles in high demand, Ukraine is increasingly relying on Western support while stepping up its own long-range strikes deep inside Russia.

Over 260 Ukrainian Children Help Foil Russian-Recruited Terror Attacks, Police Say — More than 260 Ukrainian children have contacted police and helped prevent terrorist attacks they were allegedly being recruited to carry out by Russian operatives, Ukraine’s National Police says, warning of increasingly aggressive recruitment schemes targeting minors and civilians.

Is The Kremlin Afraid of a Tiny Party? — Russia’s Supreme Court has barred the Yabloko party from September’s parliamentary elections, citing electoral-law violations. Critics say the exclusion reflects Kremlin fears that Yabloko’s anti-war message could expose opposition to the Ukraine war and challenge the narrative of broad public support. Analysts also argue Russia’s elections are already heavily manipulated and unrepresentative.

Ukraine Strikes Major Russian Oil Refinery Deep Inside Russia — Ukrainian forces struck the Orsknefteorgsintez oil refinery in Russia’s Orenburg Oblast on Aug. 11, causing a fire at one of Russia’s major oil-processing facilities. The attack came as Ukrainian forces reported strikes on dozens of Russian military and energy targets across occupied Crimea and southern Ukraine.

Syria Sentences Bashar al-Assad to Death in Absentia Over Atrocities — Syria has sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the country’s nearly 14-year civil war. His brother Maher and five other former officials were also sentenced to death in a landmark ruling by transitional authorities.

Trump Walks Back Promise to Let Ukraine Build Patriots Over Russia Fears — US President Donald Trump has backed away from plans to license Patriot missile production to Ukraine, citing concerns that sensitive technology could eventually reach Russia. The key obstacle is the missile's advanced Ka-band radar seeker, while limited production capacity and the risk of Russian strikes further complicate plans to build Patriots in Europe or Ukraine.

Kremlin Plans 70% Win for Putin’s Party in Occupied Ukraine — The Kremlin has allegedly set predetermined turnout and United Russia support target statistics for voting in occupied Ukrainian territories. Kyiv says Moscow wants to use the illegal elections to create an appearance of legitimacy for its occupation.

North Korea Arms Russia, South Korea Says No to Ukraine Weapons — South Korea is refusing to arm Ukraine despite condemning North Korea’s military support for Russia. The dispute comes after Kyiv accused Moscow of using North Korean ballistic missiles in a deadly overnight strike on Zaporizhzhia that killed six people and wounded 19.

‘Don’t Go Outside or Look Through Windows’: Russian City Locked Down for Putin Visit — Security restrictions imposed during Putin’s visit to Novosibirsk limited movement along his route and around a university campus. Residents were told to remain indoors and stay away from windows, while scooter rentals and access to parts of the city were restricted.

Europe Runs Short of Patriot Missiles as Ukraine Braces for Winter — European allies are struggling to find enough Patriot interceptors for Ukraine as Kyiv prepares for another winter of Russian missile attacks. US supplies are strained by the war in Iran, new production will not arrive in time, and several European countries say their own stocks are already too low to provide significant additional support.

Ukraine Eyes Moldova Rail Route as Russian Strikes Put Grain Exports Under Pressure — Ukraine is exploring a rail route through Moldova to Romania as Russian attacks threaten Black Sea grain exports. Kyiv has asked Chisinau for a 50% freight discount, while Moldova seeks guaranteed cargo volumes. The proposed corridor could move up to 4.5 million metric tons annually.

Fine City: ‘Territory of Freedom’ — Despite the ongoing war, the Faine Misto Festival brings thousands together in Lviv for three days of music, energy and connection. With Ukrainian and international bands taking the stage, the festival shows how music remains a source of strength and unity during wartime.

US ‘Doing Its Homework’ On Risks of Ukraine Patriot Interceptor Production — Security concerns are complicating Ukraine’s push to produce Patriot interceptors, which would still offer no quick fix for Kyiv.

Another Wildberries Warehouse Goes Up in Flames After Ukrainian Drone Strike in Russia’s Voronezh — Ukrainian drones struck Wildberries’ logistics hub in Russia’s Voronezh Oblast overnight, killing one person and sparking fires across 36,000 square meters of warehouse space. The attack marks the latest strike on Russia’s largest e-commerce platform, whose warehouses have become targets in Ukraine’s campaign against Russian logistics infrastructure.

Germany Doubles Anti-Drone Unit After Explosive Drone Breach at NATO Hub — Germany announced at a Berlin federal briefing that it will double its anti-drone police unit and expand operational bases after the Leipzig/Halle airport incident, which US intelligence reportedly links to Russia.

One Year After Alaska Summit, Trump-Putin Peace Push Fizzles as Ukraine War Escalates — A year after Trump hosted Putin in Alaska to pursue peace in Ukraine, negotiations have stalled, sanctions have returned, and both sides are escalating attacks.

Zelensky: For First Time, Russia Cannot Wage War Without North Korea — Zelensky said Russia can no longer sustain its war without North Korean support and warned that Pyongyang is gaining battlefield experience that could later threaten Japan, South Korea, and the Philippines.

US House Moves on Sweeping Russia Sanctions Bill After 86–11 Senate Vote — A bipartisan House coalition introduced the Graham sanctions package during the August recess, targeting Russian energy, banks, the shadow fleet and major buyers of Moscow’s oil.

Russian Ballistic Missile Barrage Kills 9 Across Ukraine, Kyiv Warns of North Korean Missile Support — Russian strikes killed at least nine people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight as Moscow launched a barrage of missiles, drones and guided bombs against Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Dnipropetrovsk. The attack came after Kyiv warned Russia had received new ballistic missiles from North Korea.
